messages:
alex: quick follow-up on the policy engine migration RFC. want to pick a compatibility strategy before we schedule the runtime refactor — two candidates: adapter-on-write vs in-place backward-compatible parser. thoughts?

lina: adapter-on-write seems less risky for rollout. avoids touching eval hot-path immediately. downside: we need to guarantee adapter correctness so we don't change routing semantics.

raj: +1 for adapter-on-write. implement adapter at policy-save time, emit compiled IR. runtime reads IR only. if adapter fails, keep legacy AST and mark policy as "migration_required". that minimizes branching at eval.

cheng: maintenance cost: temporarily two codepaths. we should add a migration sweep plan and deadline. also add an IR validation step to fail fast.

alex: timeline idea: week1 adapter lib + compile-on-save; week2 test harness + canary runtime; week3 expand canary and start sweep. who owns the sweep? I can coordinate with product/support for communications.

katie: please add observability: metrics for adapter_success, migrated_policy_count, ir_eval_fallbacks, and a policy_version tag on eval traces. product wants to track how many customers are on legacy rules.

raj: important semantic edge-case: DSL allowed conditionals referencing live metrics, e.g. `if p50 > 200 then prefer region=us-east weight=0.8`. IR currently supports predicates but not parametric weights. two choices: (A) synthesize discrete rules that the runtime scheduler picks between based on metric predicates, or (B) extend IR to capture parametric weights and extend scheduler.

lina: prefer (A) short-term to avoid changing scheduler. but we must document gaps in expressiveness and add tests.

cheng: testing plan: create harness that loads a corpus of ~2000 production policies, run adapter, then replay a suite of synthetic requests and compare legacy-engine vs IR decisions. surface diffs by policy id and rule hit counts. include property tests for threshold boundaries.

alex: also ensure a robust fallback: runtime should catch IR eval errors and fallback to legacy engine with metric `ir_fallback=1`. do not fail requests in that case.

katie: UX: console should show migration status per-policy, adapter error details, and a one-click re-run migrate action. when migrate fails, provide a suggested fix link to the RFC examples. support will thank us.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for policy-adapter v0.1 on 2026-04-02 04:00 UTC.

incident-bot: reference note: INC-2025-11 involved parser bug under high concurrency causing 504s. make sure adapter load-time work does not trigger similar path that touches runtime. migration must be async from eval hot-path.

raj: implementation checklist (short bullets):
- adapter library (policy -> IR)
- IR schema with versioning and backward compatibility notes
- compile-on-save endpoint (PUT /policies/:id/compile)
- migration state on policy metadata (migrated|migration_required|migration_failed)
- metrics: adapter_success, migrated_count, ir_eval_fallback
- test harness + property tests for numeric thresholds
- canary runtime switch and graceful fallback

alex: code sketch for adapter output (pseudo-JSON string for readability):
```
{
  "policy_id": "p-42",
  "ir_version": "2026-04-v1",
  "rules": [
    { "match": {"region": "us-east", "tier": "pro"}, "action": {"prefer": "low_latency", "weight": "parametric(p50, 200, 0.9)"} }
  ]
}
```

lina: since IR currently doesn't support `parametric(...)`, adapter should expand that into multiple concrete rules for runtime to select between. add a ticket to track IR feature to natively support parametric weights.

cheng: compatibility notes: store original policy blob alongside compiled IR to allow human review and rollback. include a migration-audit log entry each time adapter runs.

katie: minor: add admin endpoint to force recompile for a policy and to bulk recompile a set filtered by tag (e.g., exported-by:customer-team).

alex: ok locking in plan. i'll open the follow-up RFC update and assign tasks. target: start work next sprint, aim for canary within ~3 weeks. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
